In [[mathematics]], the '''Contou-Carrère symbol''' 〈''a'',''b''〉 is a [[Steinberg symbol]] defined on pairs of [[Unit (ring theory)|invertible elements]] of the ring of [[Laurent series|Laurent power series]] over an [[Artinian ring]] ''k'', taking values in the group of units of ''k''. It was introduced by {{harvtxt|Contou-Carrère|1994}}.

==Definition==

If ''k'' is an Artinian local ring, then any invertible formal Laurent series ''a'' with coefficients in ''k'' can be written uniquely as
:<math>a=a_0t^{w(a)}\prod_{i\ne 0}(1-a_it^i)</math>
where ''w''(''a'') is an integer, the elements ''a''<sub>''i''</sub> are in ''k'', and are in ''m'' if ''i'' is negative, and is a unit if ''i''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.

The Contou-Carrère symbol 〈''a'',''b''〉 of ''a'' and ''b'' is defined to be
:<math>\langle a,b\rangle=(-1)^{w(a)w(b)}\frac{a_0^{w(b)}\prod_{i,j>0}(1-a_i^{j/(i,j)}b_{-j}^{i/(i,j)})^{(i,j)}}
{b_0^{w(a)}\prod_{i,j>0}(1-b_i^{j/(i,j)}a_{-j}^{i/(i,j)})^{(i,j)}}</math>
